name: Guiyang Longdongbao International Airport
before:
Guizhou's gateway, 11 km south east of Guiyang, and busier than most people expect: just over 30.2 million passengers in 2025, which makes it the twenty third busiest airport in mainland China.

Getting into the city is easy in two different ways. A metro station on Line 2 serves the terminal directly, and there is a railway station underneath the airport itself, so onward travel into the province does not need a road transfer at all.

The runway is 3,200 metres and takes wide bodies up to a 747 or an A330. The terminal covers around 34,000 square metres and is rated for more than two thousand passengers an hour in each direction.

It is the hub for Colorful Guizhou Airlines. The airport opened in 1997 and took its current name in 2006, and has been expanding more or less continuously since it passed its original five million passenger design capacity in 2010.
after:
The airport for Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou province, sits 11 km south east of the city centre. It handled 22.7 million passengers in 2025, the twenty third highest total in mainland China.

Rail links are good. Guiyang Metro Line 2 has run to the airport since April 2021, and high-speed trains call at Longdongbao railway station, which serves the airport.

There are two runways, the longer at 4,000 metres, and the airport is the base for Colorful Guizhou Airlines. Commercial flights began on 28 May 1997.
